synthesis: GET /api/scout/dashboard/check-in-counts (ScoutCheckInRollupQuery) returns {direct_bucket:0, staging_bucket:0} for every kit because its `addresses` CTE sources candidate open-assignment addresses from clarity.recovery_address (a repossession-only MV) INNER JOINed to Open hotlists. Open hotlists almost never have a recovery_address row, so ~0 addresses match. Fix: repoint the CTE to the real open-assignment path clarity.hotlist(status=Open) -> zod.public_hotlist_address -> zod.public_address, parse EWKT geo, guard nulls/(0,0), preserve the proximity matcher + hour-bucket dedup + is_staged split + staging-org auth, and re-fixture the tests onto the two zod tables. The sibling HotlistAddressGeohashQuery already implements this exact join+parse idiom and is the pattern to mirror.

scope.summary: Repoint ScoutCheckInRollupQuery's addresses CTE from clarity.recovery_address to zod.public_hotlist_address->zod.public_address (Open hotlists), using the repo's established extract()+toFloat64OrNull EWKT parse and id-IN-subquery (never a JOIN on public_address), plus a scan-window-derived performance prefilter (approach pending gate answer), and re-fixture the Feature tests onto the two zod tables.

proposed_changes.change: Rewrite the `addresses` CTE (47-62): select address ids for Open (+authorized staging) hotlists via `zod.public_hotlist_address.address_id IN (subquery over clarity.hotlist FINAL status=1 with existing hotlistOrgFilter)`, resolve coords from `zod.public_address` filtered by `a.id IN (...)` (no JOIN), parse geo via toFloat64OrNull(extract(a.geo,'POINT ?\(([-0-9.]+) ')) / extract(a.geo,' ([-0-9.]+)\)'), guard geo NULL/''/(0,0), carry hl.is_staged through. Add the agreed perf prefilter (bbox from the kit's scan-window extent). No FINAL on the zod tables (matcher DISTINCT + _peerdb_is_deleted=0 absorb dup versions, per sibling convention).
proposed_changes.reason: recovery_address is repossession-only; open-assignment addresses live in public_hotlist_address->public_address. Mirror HotlistAddressGeohashQuery's deliberate perf/parse choices.

questions.q: Performance approach for the scans x open-addresses geoDistance matcher on high-volume kits (bbox vs geohash-prefix vs narrow-only)
questions.answer: Scan-window bbox prefilter: compute the kit's scan-window lat/lng extent (min/max over the kit's scans in the window) and prefilter candidate open-addresses to that bounding box before the geoDistance join, reusing the HotlistAddressGeohashQuery bbox idiom. (Dalton deferred to recommendation.)

notes: CORRECTION to ticket: do NOT use readWKTPoint (ticket suggests it) — it throws on malformed/non-POINT rows and ClickhouseQuery::query() swallows the exception to []; use extract()+toFloat64OrNull like HotlistAddressGeohashQuery.php:124-133.
Never JOIN zod.public_address (~189M rows) — use `a.id IN (subquery)` (rides id PK). HotlistAddressGeohashQuery.php:120-152.
Skip FINAL on the two zod tables; rely on _peerdb_is_deleted=0 + the matcher's DISTINCT (address_id,is_staged,hour_bucket). Sibling convention.
ClickhouseQuery::query() swallows exceptions to report()+[] in prod/testing — a timeout looks identical to the original bug (silent empty). Raises the stakes on the perf approach (AC5).
